# RHEL 8 GCC Toolset 12 Toolchain v1.0.1

Maintenance release focused on release reproducibility, immutable distribution, and end-to-end compatibility validation. The compiler/runtime compatibility model and ABI policy are unchanged from v1.0.0.

## Highlights

- GCC 12.4 compiler and modern C++20 headers from conda-forge.
- glibc 2.28 sysroot baseline.
- RHEL 8 / GCC 8-era shared `libstdc++.so.6` and `libgcc_s.so.1`.
- GCC Toolset 12.2.1 `libstdc++_nonshared.a` compatibility layer.
- Compiler environment variables use compatibility wrappers without replacing the user's `gcc`, `g++`, or normal `PATH` command resolution.

Release ABI policy remains:

```text
GLIBC   <= 2.28
GLIBCXX <= 3.4.25
CXXABI  <= 1.3.11
GCC ABI <= 7.0.0
```

## Release engineering improvements

### Immutable production conda channel

The production channel is now published only from immutable semantic-version tags.

- `main`, pull requests, and manual validation builds use an unpublished `0.0.0` candidate.
- A tag such as `v1.0.1` renders custom conda package version `1.0.1`.
- Release publication seeds the new channel snapshot from the currently published channel.
- Reusing an existing `name + version + build number` is rejected.
- Existing package artifacts remain part of the published channel snapshot.

### Behavior-derived Action identity

The Action cache identity now includes behavior-affecting inputs in addition to the manifest and explicit package lock, including assembly/activation logic and metadata normalization. Compiler or linker policy changes therefore invalidate consumer caches even when package inputs remain unchanged.

### Metadata consistency gate

CI now verifies that the manifest, explicit conda locks, and exact conda recipe requirements agree before toolchain assembly.

### Fully pinned conda channel builder

The rattler-build environment is now recreated from the SHA-256-pinned `manifests/conda-builder-linux-64.lock` explicit lock instead of being solved from a version-only constraint.

### AlmaLinux 8 runtime execution gate

Representative C and C++20 probes are compiled with the compatibility wrappers and then actually executed inside a digest-pinned AlmaLinux 8 amd64 container.

This complements the existing ELF, symbol-version, linker-selection, ownership, RPATH, and activation/deactivation verification.

## Install with micromamba

```bash
micromamba create -y -n rhel8-gcc-toolset12 \
  --override-channels \
  -c https://edgeatzero.github.io/rhel8-gcc-toolset12-toolchain/conda \
  -c conda-forge \
  --strict-channel-priority \
  rhel8-gcc-toolset12-toolchain=1.0.1

micromamba activate rhel8-gcc-toolset12
```

Published conda package builds:

```text
rhel8-gcc-toolset12-compat      1.0.1 build 1
rhel8-gcc-toolset12-activate    1.0.1 build 3
rhel8-gcc-toolset12-toolchain   1.0.1 build 2
```

## GitHub Action

Recommended stable v1 reference:

```yaml
- uses: EdgeAtZero/rhel8-gcc-toolset12-toolchain@v1
```

Immutable pin:

```yaml
- uses: EdgeAtZero/rhel8-gcc-toolset12-toolchain@v1.0.1
```

## Distribution

The GitHub Release remains source-only. The assembled third-party GCC/binutils/glibc/sysroot runtime toolchain is not attached as a Release asset. The public conda channel installs the compatibility packages while obtaining the pinned conda-forge dependencies from their original channel.

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/EdgeAtZero/rhel8-gcc-toolset12-toolchain/compare/v1.0.0...v1.0.1
